faq.q: What formula does it use and what does the EMI exclude?
faq.a: It uses the standard reducing-balance EMI formula, P × r × (1+r)ⁿ ÷ ((1+r)ⁿ − 1), where r is the annual rate ÷ 12 ÷ 100 and n is months. It's an estimate of principal and interest only — the disclaimer notes your actual EMI also depends on processing fees, insurance, GST and your credit profile, so confirm with the lender before signing.

faq.q: Are the loan-type presets the real interest rates?
faq.a: No. The Home, Car, Personal, Education, Gold, Two-wheeler and Business presets just load typical default amounts, rates and tenures as a starting point (e.g. Home 8.5% over 20 years). The tool states plainly these are indicative only and your bank's offer may differ — adjust the sliders to your actual figures.

faq.q: Can I get a full month-by-month schedule?
faq.a: The page shows a year-wise summary table and charts, but the PDF and CSV exports carry the complete month-by-month repayment schedule — each instalment's EMI, principal, interest and remaining balance, with the final instalment adjusted so the balance lands exactly on zero. The PDF uses 'Rs.' rather than the rupee symbol due to font limits. For prepayment analysis, it points you to the separate Loan Calculator.

faq.q: How does the Affordability Helper decide what I can afford?
faq.a: Enter your monthly income and any existing EMIs and it applies the common lender rule of thumb — total EMIs of 40–50% of income — showing a comfortable maximum (40% minus existing EMIs) and a stretch maximum (50%), then flags whether your current EMI fits. It's labelled guidance, not financial advice. Your inputs are autosaved in your browser under emiState.
